jobs.title: Director, Risk and Performance Technology
jobs.description:
At IMCO, our talent is among the best! IMCO offers a uniquely stimulating and rewarding environment where you can help build and drive organizational transformation, all while seeking to challenge yourself, learn, and grow your career.

Our culture is built on collaboration and passion, with a shared commitment to delivering lasting value to the clients we serve. Located in downtown Toronto, our vision is to be the partner of choice for Ontario’s public sector funds and to build a high-performing, value-driven asset management firm.

This job posting is for an existing vacancy. If you are ready to deliver best-in-class service and join a collaborative, motivated and fun team of professionals, IMCO offers the opportunity to do impactful work and broaden your expertise.

If you’re looking to use your expertise to drive strategic outcomes, we’d love to hear from you.

‎

As IMCO continues to evolve its Target Operating Model, the importance of timely, trusted, and actionable risk and performance insights continues to grow. Technology plays a critical role in enabling investment decision-making, performance measurement, portfolio analytics, regulatory reporting, and enterprise risk oversight.

If you are looking to lead a strategic technology portfolio and help shape the future of Risk and Performance capabilities at IMCO, we would love to hear from you.

We are looking for a highly motivated Director, Risk & Performance Technology.

Reporting to the Vice President, Investment Technology, the Director, Risk & Performance Technology is accountable for the strategy, delivery, operation, and evolution of IMCO's Risk and Performance technology capabilities.

This role provides technology leadership for the applications, analytical platforms, reporting capabilities, and integrations that support Risk and Performance. The Director will establish the roadmap for the Risk and Performance technology portfolio, lead key technology initiatives, and ensure technology capabilities remain scalable, reliable, and aligned with IMCO's future operating model.

The role partners closely with Risk, Performance, Investment Operations, Data & AI Enablement, Enterprise Technology, and Front Office stakeholders to improve analytical capabilities, enhance reporting and measurement processes, and deliver trusted insights across the organization.

Key Responsibilities:

Technology Strategy & Business Partnership

Define and execute the multi-year technology roadmap for Risk and Performance capabilities, ensuring alignment with business priorities and IMCO's Target Operating Model.
Serve as a trusted technology advisor to leaders across Risk and Performance.
Partner with business stakeholders to identify future capability needs, technology opportunities, and process improvement initiatives.
Contribute to Investment Technology planning activities and support the development of long-term technology strategies across the investment ecosystem.
Support business case development, vendor evaluations, and technology investment decisions related to Risk and Performance platforms.

Risk & Performance Solution Delivery

Lead the delivery and enhancement of technology solutions supporting portfolio risk measurement, factor analytics, exposure analysis, performance measurement, attribution, benchmark management, and investment reporting.
Oversee the design, implementation, integration, and support of business-critical applications and analytical platforms.
Ensure solutions are designed to support scalability, automation, operational efficiency, and future business growth.
Partner with Architecture, Data Platform & AI Engineering, Enterprise Technology, and Cyber Security teams to ensure alignment with enterprise standards and target architectures.
Promote effective delivery practices and ensure technology solutions are implemented in a disciplined and sustainable manner.

Application Portfolio Ownership

Provide overall ownership and oversight of Risk and Performance technology platforms and application portfolios.
Establish application roadmaps, lifecycle management plans, and support strategies that align with business objectives.
Lead application upgrades, enhancements, integrations, modernization initiatives, and platform rationalization activities.
Evaluate emerging vendor solutions and analytical capabilities to support evolving business requirements.
Manage strategic relationships with software vendors, implementation partners, and service providers.

Data, Analytics & Reporting Enablement

Partner with the Data Platform & AI Engineering team and business stakeholders to ensure Risk and Performance solutions leverage trusted, governed, and reconciled investment data.
Support the development and consumption of analytical data products, calculation engines, and reporting-ready datasets.
Drive improvements in measurement processes, reporting workflows, calculation transparency, and analytical consistency.
Promote the adoption of common data standards and integrated analytical capabilities across investment teams.
Enable modern analytics, reporting, and decision-support capabilities that improve investment insight and business outcomes.

Governance & Operational Excellence

Ensure Risk and Performance technology solutions operate in accordance with IMCO policies, architecture standards, security requirements, and governance frameworks.
Establish operational processes that support stable, secure, and sustainable application services.
Oversee incident, problem, change, release, and service management activities across the portfolio.
Support audits, risk assessments, compliance reviews, and control testing activities.
Ensure appropriate documentation, training materials, support procedures, and operational controls are maintained.

People Leadership

Build and lead a high-performing team of business analysts, application specialists, technical leads, and technology professionals.
Foster a culture of innovation, collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Coach, mentor, and develop team members to support career growth and organizational capability development.
Establish clear objectives, performance expectations, and development plans aligned with business and technology goals.

What you need to succeed:

12+ years of progressive experience delivering and supporting investment technology solutions within asset management, investment management, or financial services environments.
Demonstrated success leading technology teams supporting Risk, Performance, Analytics, or related investment functions.
Strong understanding of portfolio risk management, performance measurement and attribution, benchmark management, investment reporting, and portfolio analytics.
Experience developing technology roadmaps and delivering complex application and platform initiatives.
Strong knowledge of investment data, analytical platforms, reporting solutions, and application integration patterns.
Experience managing software vendors, implementation partners, and managed service providers.
Familiarity with Agile, Waterfall, and hybrid delivery methodologies.
Strong understanding of application lifecycle management, service management, governance, and operational support practices.
Excellent communication, relationship management, and stakeholder engagement skills.
Experience with industry-leading Risk and Performance platforms such as MSCI RiskManager, BarraOne, Axioma, FactSet, Bloomberg PORT, Eagle Performance, or similar solutions is highly desirable.
Undergraduate degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Finance, Mathematics, or a related field. Advanced education and professional certifications are considered an asset.

‎

We thank all applicants for their interest. Only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

Our hybrid work model prioritizes an office-first approach, encouraging employees to make the most of our collaborative workspace at 16 York Street, Suite 2400, Toronto, ON M5J 0E6. This welcoming environment fosters teamwork, connection, and professional growth. While flexibility remains a key component of our model, we believe that regular in-office engagement enhances productivity and strengthens our culture. jobs.title: Associate Director, Development Analytics (Sales and Fundraising Analytics)
jobs.description:
About Us

SickKids Foundation, with over 50 years of philanthropic impact is Canada's largest charitable funder of child health research, learning and care, raising over $200 million last year. As a national charity, SickKids Foundation invests in national and international initiatives to benefit children in Canada and around the world. As the fundraising partner to The Hospital for Sick Children (SickKids), we are aligned in supporting Precision Child Health (PCH), the future of tailoring medicine to each child's unique traits so SickKids can diagnose faster, treat smarter, and predict better.

We are driven by our core values of integrity, collaboration, excellence, innovation, and inclusion, with goals of delivering a superior donor experience, investing in our people and culture, driving innovative and sustainable fundraising, and disrupting the market through data and technology.

SickKids Foundation is committed to an inclusive culture by embedding equity, diversity and inclusion in our policies, practices, and behaviours. We aim to build awareness and skills in this area, both internally and with our partners. Our commitment extends to creating a safe, positive work environment. For details on our Equity, Diversity & Inclusion commitment, please click here.

We’re committed to attracting and retaining passionate individuals to help create a healthier future. That’s why SickKids Foundation is looking for a new Associate Director, Development Analytics.

Description Of The Position

Fundraising is a sales function. It has a pipeline, defined stages, conversion rates, cycle times and coverage ratios—and a frontline team whose time is one of the organization’s scarcest resources.

The Associate Director, Development Analytics owns the analytics behind that pipeline. The role makes fundraising performance visible and measurable, identifies where opportunities exist to improve it, and translates those insights into clear, actionable recommendations for fundraising leaders.

This is a hands-on role for a sales and pipeline analytics professional. The successful candidate is comfortable working directly with data, building reporting and dashboards, and developing analytical or predictive models when they add value. But the role goes beyond producing reports and models. Its real value is in the analysis: knowing which metrics matter, identifying where the pipeline is performing well or breaking down, uncovering opportunities within fundraiser portfolios, and helping leaders understand what actions they can take as a result.

The role also connects Research Services with frontline fundraising. It translates prospect intelligence and analytical signals into clear, prioritized opportunities so fundraisers can focus their time and effort on the prospects with the greatest potential.

The Associate Director, Development Analytics is a key role within the Business Intelligence & Analytics team. Reporting directly to the Director, Development Analytics, you will provide functional leadership for Development Analytics, serve as the authoritative advisor to Development leadership, and partner across the analytics function: with Data Science & Engineering to ensure development data is well modelled and accessible, with Research Services to turn prospect intelligence into action, and with Marketing Analytics to build end-to-end visibility from donor acquisition through the development pipeline.

You will play a central role in delivering the Foundation's Data & Analytics Strategy (DAS) for Development, setting the analytics roadmap, standards and priorities and executing key use cases that build analytics maturity and drive measurable value for fundraising and the broader organization.

Key Responsibilities

Functional Leadership & Roadmap

Provide functional leadership for Development Analytics, integrating pipeline, portfolio, revenue, campaign and donor analytics across Development.
Establish and maintain the Development Analytics roadmap, operating model, methodologies, standards and tools within the approved Development strategy and the DAS.
Own the development analytics intake process: prioritize, approve, defer or redirect analytics requests so that priorities are clear, timelines are met and the team is set up to deliver with consistency and quality.
Serve as the authoritative advisor to Development leadership on forecasting, portfolio optimization, prospect strategy, performance measurement and the effective allocation of fundraising resources.
Maintain and enforce analytics processes and standards, and hold stakeholders accountable for agreed data inputs and business requirements.
Measure and report on the adoption and impact of analytics products.
Resolve conflicting business requirements, data limitations and competing analytical priorities across Development, determining when existing approaches should be adapted or replaced.
Anticipate emerging business needs and initiate analytical work that may challenge current assumptions, practices or resource-allocation decisions.

Pipeline, Portfolio & Performance Analytics

Own development pipeline analytics: stage progression, conversion and win rates, cycle time and velocity, coverage ratios, average gift size and slippage, by fundraiser, portfolio, segment and campaign.
Independently identify and frame where the funnel is underperforming and why, including emerging issues where the problem and approach are not yet defined, and bring forward specific, prioritized recommendations rather than describing the numbers.
Partner with fundraising leadership on portfolio construction and optimization: right-sizing portfolios, balancing prospect capacity against fundraiser bandwidth, surfacing under-worked or misassigned prospects, and analyzing frontline productivity to improve return on fundraiser time.
Establish Development-wide KPI definitions and analytical standards for pipeline, portfolio, revenue and fundraiser-performance reporting, within enterprise data-governance requirements, so leadership, Finance and the lines of business work from one trusted set of numbers.
Build, maintain and evolve self-serve dashboards and automated reporting tools that allow fundraising teams to access portfolio insights and performance data independently to make faster decisions.
Translate complex findings into clear narratives, presentations and recommendations for non-technical audiences.

Advanced Analytics & Predictive Modelling

Build and deploy predictive models such as propensity to give, upgrade likelihood, lapse prediction, segmentation and lifetime value (LTV) to inform portfolio strategy, prospect prioritization and the allocation of fundraising resources.
Lead revenue forecasting and in-year reforecasting with weighted pipeline analysis and scenario modelling, clearly articulating risk and upside.
Work with Research Services to translate prospect intelligence and wealth screening into scoring, ranked prospect pools and prioritized opportunities that fundraisers can act on directly.
Design and execute deep dive analyses to answer key business questions, including pipeline conversion, portfolio health, upgrade and retention drivers, and return on fundraiser time.
Partner with Data Science & Engineering to ensure development data is well modelled and accessible through reliable source tables and curated data marts, and approve routine changes to dashboards, models and analytical processes.

Team Leadership & Coaching

Lead, coach and actively upskill analysts and assigned resources in analytical thinking, data storytelling and stakeholder communication, building the capabilities needed to position the team as trusted strategic partners to the business.
Create a culture of curiosity, quality and continuous improvement by generously sharing knowledge across the team, introducing better ways to approach data analysis, building models and interpreting findings to raise the overall quality of analytical output.
Allocate the capacity of analysts and assigned resources across competing priorities, making clear decisions about what gets resourced, deferred or escalated, and recommend investments and staffing requirements based on identified functional needs.
Foster a collaborative and inclusive team environment that reflects SickKids Foundation's values of integrity, collaboration, excellence, innovation and inclusion.

What We Are Looking For

Bachelor’s degree in Statistics, Economics, Business, Computer Science or related field; Master’s degree an asset.
7+ years of experience in sales, pipeline, funnel, revenue or fundraising analytics, directly supporting a revenue-generating frontline team.
Demonstrable understanding of how a sales funnel works in practice: stages, qualification, coverage, conversion, forecasting discipline and why deals stall. This may come from a commercial or a philanthropic setting.
Advanced knowledge of fundraising strategy and operations, predictive analytics, forecasting, data governance and statistical modelling, with the ability to integrate these disciplines into an effective Development-wide analytics function.
Strong hands-on experience with Databricks or a similar cloud platform, SQL, Power BI, and at least one analytical or modelling tool (Python, R, SAS).
Proven track record building and deploying predictive models including segmentation, propensity scoring, LTV, or lapse prediction.
3+ years of experience leading or mentoring a team of analysts, including setting analytics priorities, standards and roadmaps.
Experience designing and building self-serve dashboards and automated reporting frameworks.
Demonstrated ability to work with CRM systems; Salesforce experience is a strong asset.
Experience in fundraising, prospect research, wealth screening or moves management is an asset.
Experience applying GenAI tooling to analytics or research workflows is an advantage.

Total Compensation Package

Expected Hiring Salary Range:
$99,297 - $124,121; with the ability to progress to a maximum of $142,739 with demonstrated experience and proficiency. To ensure fair and equitable pay at SickKids Foundation, placement on the salary range will be based on your years of experience, skills, and qualifications relevant to the Associate Director, Development Analytics.

To help you lead in the fight for kids’ health and to support your health, wellness, and career growth, in addition to competitive compensation, we offer a comprehensive benefit package (includes a flex benefit plan), tuition reimbursement, flexible work arrangements, pension plan and birth parent/parental top up – to name a few!

Lead financial and corporate stewardship for Curve Lake First Nation

Step into a senior leadership role offering a competitive $150,000 to $180,000 annual salary, negotiable based on qualifications, plus excellent benefits!

Build the systems, teams, and financial stability that will support the Nation for the next decade

About Curve Lake First Nation

Curve Lake First Nation is an Anishinaabe community with deep roots in this territory, grounded in relationships to land, water, and each other as Curve Lakers. Known historically as Mud Lake, Curve Lake continues as a living, resilient Nation of almost 3,000 members. As part of the Michi Saagiig Anishinaabeg and signatories to the Williams Treaties, the community carries forward its responsibilities, teachings, and governance systems. Curve Lake is a place of strong kinship, cultural continuity, and collective responsibility, where each member contributes to the wellbeing of the Nation. Our community is located just north of the City of Peterborough, Ontario.

Home to trailblazers like Elsie Knott, Canada's first Anishinaabe Kwe O'gimaa, and renowned artisans, our community blends rich history with vibrant culture. More than an employer, we're a community of choice. Join us in preserving traditions, fostering diversity, and contributing to a future where old ways merge seamlessly with progress. Shape the legacy of Curve Lake—a place where heritage meets opportunity.

To learn more about us, please visit: curvelakefirstnation.ca

About the Opportunity

Curve Lake First Nation has an exciting opportunity for a full-time, permanent Director of Finance and Administration
, based in Curve Lake, Ontario.
This role joins the organization during a period of organizational transition and growth.

Reporting to the Executive Director, you will provide strategic leadership across the Nation’s corporate functions. These are financial governance, human resources, policy and planning, communications, and information technology. Finance sits at the heart of the role. You will be accountable for sound financial oversight, audit readiness, and strong relationships with funders, auditors, and the First Nations Financial Management Board.

Where We Are Now

The Nation is strengthening its administrative foundations; you will provide interim oversight and stabilization across Finance, HR, IT, and Policy and Planning while building out your team. You will also lead the selection and implementation of a new Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system.

A key priority is moving the Nation from year-by-year funding to Indigenous Services Canada’s 10-year grant. This means completing the Financial Management Board certification process and putting the controls and reporting in place to qualify. Predictable, long-term funding will give the Nation far greater confidence in its forecasting and planning.

What Success Looks Like

In your first year, success will mean a fully staffed division with your managers in place, trusted relationships with Chief and Council, staff, and community, strengthened audit readiness and internal controls, and the ERP selection well underway.

By the end of year two, you will have led the Nation through FMB certification and embedded consistent financial, governance, and administrative practices. You will also have put systems in place that keep reporting and audits on schedule, giving the organization a solid foundation for the years ahead.

Your responsibilities include, but are not limited to:
Leading multi-year financial planning, forecasting, and annual operating and capital budgets
Serving as executive lead for external audits, including selecting the appropriate audit firm and working closely with auditors throughout the process
Ensuring compliance with funding agreements, Indigenous Services Canada reporting requirements, and the Nation’s Financial Administration Law
Leading the Nation through the FMB certification and 10-year grant process
Structuring and staffing the finance function so reporting deadlines are consistently met, working with bookkeepers, analysts, and account managers
Providing executive oversight of HR, IT, policy and planning, and communications through four direct-report managers
Overseeing the selection and implementation of an ERP system, along with cybersecurity, data governance, and digital modernization
Providing financial analysis, risk advice, and recommendations to the Executive Director and Chief and Council

Due to the role's significance, refer to the Director of Finance and Administration document for a comprehensive overview beyond the listed duties.

More About You

To qualify, you will need a post-secondary degree or diploma in finance, accounting, or a related financial field
, along with at least 5 years of senior-level experience in financial administration or corporate services,
including experience working within a First Nation organization.

The following are required:
A valid Class G Driver’s Licence
Ability to undergo a criminal background check and vulnerable sector check
Willingness and ability to travel as required

The following skills and experience will be strong assets:
Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation
Certified Aboriginal Financial Manager (CAFM) or Certified Aboriginal Professional Administrator (CAPA) designation
A master’s degree in public administration, finance, or a related field
Direct experience with the First Nations Financial Management Board, FMB certification, or the 10-year grant process
Strong working knowledge of audit processes, GAAP, and funder reporting requirements
Experience working with Indigenous Services Canada and other funding agencies
Experience overseeing multiple functional areas such as Finance, HR, IT, and Planning

As our ideal candidate, you are a disciplined, systems-minded leader who keeps deadlines met and audits clean, and who knows how to build a finance team organized around its reporting obligations. Your understanding of First Nation finances runs from day-to-day funding agreements through to the path toward long-term grant funding. Just as importantly, you lead with integrity, calm, and a people-centred approach, bringing an awareness of intergenerational trauma and its impact on workplaces and governance, along with a genuine respect for Curve Lake First Nation’s history, culture, and traditions.

Note: Preference will be given to applicants who have First Nation or Indigenous ancestry.

About the Benefits

negotiable dependent on experience, along with a great host of benefits, including:
Relocation assistance

Regular community events such as Pow Wows, Harvesters' Gatherings, Christmas Craft Shows, and more!

Le programme d'avions commerciaux A220 recherche un Leader en amélioration des données pour rejoindre notre équipe Performance Management basée à Mirabel (Québec, Canada), où vous collaborez étroitement avec les analystes de performance, les équipes des Opérations et l'équipe de digitalisation.

Vous ferez partie de l’équipe Performance Management chargée de développer la standardisation et l'amélioration de la qualité des données de performance pour la chaîne de valeur A220, tout en soutenant la feuille de route de digitalisation. L'organisation de l'équipe est établie de manière à promouvoir la collaboration transversale et l'autonomie, dans un esprit de soutien mutuel et d'apprentissage collectif.

Dans ce rôle, vous agirez en tant que point de contact central et facilitateur entre les analystes de la performance opérationnelle et l'équipe de digitalisation. Garantir la qualité, la cohérence et l'exactitude des données de performance issues des flux d'approvisionnement et de production;

As a top 10 global dairy processor, we value contributions that matter and strive to foster an inclusive, growth-driven work environment. Ready to bring your best?

Overview of the role:

Saputo is seeking a Senior Director, Revenue Management – North America.

The Senior Director, Revenue Management leads Saputo North America’s revenue management agenda across Canada and the United States to deliver sustainable, profitable growth across customers, channels, categories, and products. This role integrates pricing, trade investment, promotion effectiveness, mix and assortment, and portfolio profitability into one disciplined commercial framework. The Senior Director partners with Sales, Marketing, Finance, Supply Chain, Operations, Category & Product Management, Commercial R&D, and Technology to translate market, customer, commodity, and cost dynamics into fact-based decisions and consistent execution.

As a senior commercial thought leader, the Senior Director establishes governance, analytics, tools, and decision forums that improve pricing accuracy, strengthen return on trade investment, accelerate insights, and build an integrated revenue management capability across Saputo North America while enabling market-specific execution in Canada and the United States.

How you will make contributions that matter:

Revenue Management Strategy & Governance

Own and evolve the Saputo North America revenue management strategy, operating model, multi-year roadmap, and performance scorecard in alignment with business and commercial priorities.
Integrate the core revenue growth levers of pricing, promotions, trade terms, mix, assortment, channel strategy, and portfolio optimization.
Align North American standards with country-specific market conditions, customer structures, commercial practices, and business priorities to drive consistency without limiting local agility.
Establish decision rights, approval thresholds, guardrails, and governance for pricing, trade investment, promotions, bids, contracts, and new business opportunities.
Define clear North American and country-level decision rights, escalation paths, and accountability across the Canadian and U.S. businesses.
Lead pricing and revenue management forums, ensuring decisions, assumptions, risks, approvals, and follow-up actions are documented and communicated.
Serve as a trusted advisor to senior Sales, Finance, Category & Product, Marketing, Operations, and Supply Chain leaders, constructively challenging assumptions and recommending action.

Pricing Strategy, Architecture & Execution

Lead market-based pricing strategies that reflect commodity movements, inflation, supply chain costs, cost-to-serve, competitive dynamics, and customer value.
Oversee periodic and event-driven price reviews, scenario modeling, financial evaluation, sales materials, customer transition plans, and execution of approved price changes.
Develop and maintain price corridors, floors, exception protocols, validation controls, and pricing policies that improve consistency and reduce value leakage.
Optimize ERP-enabled price data, maintenance routines, and controls to improve pricing accuracy, transparency, and monthly price-change execution.
Partner with Sales on complex negotiations and customer conversations, balancing profitable growth, customer needs, and volume risk.

Trade Investment & Promotion Effectiveness

Own the governance and optimization of total trade investment, including planning standards, approval criteria, accrual alignment, performance tracking, and post-event review.
Establish consistent pre- and post-promotion evaluation methods using incremental volume, revenue, margin, return on investment, and strategic objectives.
Identify non-productive spend, value leakage, and underperforming events; partner with commercial teams to redirect investment toward higher-return opportunities.
Maintain promotional guidelines and embed lessons learned into customer plans, annual planning, and future investment decisions.

Customer, Channel & Portfolio Profitability

Lead recurring diagnostics across Canada and the United States, including customers, channels, categories, brands, and SKUs to identify performance drivers, risks, and corrective actions.
Advance category and portfolio profitability by prioritizing opportunities in mix, assortment, product rationalization, and route-to-market economics.
Develop actions for the highest- and lowest-performing customers and SKUs, including margin improvement, cost-to-serve, terms, freight, and commercialization opportunities.
Create clear North American executive reporting that connects price, volume, mix, trade, freight, currency, and cost movements to net sales and margin outcomes, with visibility to consolidated and country-level performance.

New Business, Bids & Commercial Decision Support

Support the financial and strategic evaluation of bids, new customers, private label, co-manufacturing, innovation, and other business development opportunities.
Apply defined guardrails and scenario analysis to assess profitability, capacity, factory utilization, service requirements, risk, and incremental growth.
Maintain scalable bid and tender tools, decision records, and post-launch scorecards to confirm performance against approved business cases.

Planning, Forecasting & Performance Management

Co-lead North American net sales and customer margin planning with Sales Operations and Finance, including consolidated, country, channel, customer, category, and product views.
Lead in-year forecasting and scenario planning for price, volume, mix, trade, freight, commodity exposure, and customer margin performance.
Provide timely diagnostics for weekly, monthly, quarterly, and annual business reviews, highlighting causals, outlook, risks, opportunities, and recommended actions.
Partner with Finance on close-related revenue management activities, including customer expense classification, true-ups, pricing factors, and relevant commodity or hedging impacts.

Data, Digital Enablement & Advanced Analytics

Define the North American revenue management data, reporting, and technology roadmap, including ERP, trade promotion, customer, syndicated market,.
Improve data quality, common definitions, master data, model governance, and controls so leaders can make decisions from trusted information.
Harmonize revenue management definitions, performance measures, and reporting across Canada and the United States to enable comparable insights and coordinated decision-making.
Champion responsible use of advanced analytics, automation, and AI-enabled decision support for elasticity, scenario modeling, promotion optimization, forecasting, and opportunity identification.
Ensure analytical methods remain explainable, validated, appropriately governed, and paired with commercial judgment.
Drive adoption of self-service dashboards and standardized tools while preserving clear accountability for decisions and outcomes.

10+ years of progressive experience in revenue management, commercial finance, sales operations, pricing, category management, or a related commercial discipline.
Leadership experience in consumer-packaged goods, food and beverage, dairy, or another complex, customer-driven manufacturing environment.
Bachelor’s degree in business, Finance, Economics, Marketing, Analytics, Supply Chain, or related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience. Master's degree or advanced professional qualification in Business, Finance, Analytics, or a related field, is preferred.
Demonstrated experience leading teams and influencing senior cross-functional stakeholders.
Demonstrated ability to lead through a matrixed, multi-country organization and influence senior stakeholders across Canada and the United States.
Deep experience in pricing, trade investment, promotion analytics, customer profitability, forecasting, and commercial decision support.
Experience translating complex data into clear recommendations, business cases, and executable commercial actions.
Working knowledge of commodity- and cost-driven pricing dynamics, customer negotiations, and commercialization processes.
Experience with ERP and commercial analytics environments; ability to lead processes, data, and technology improvement.
Experience with SAP and trade promotion, pricing, syndicated data, visualization, and advanced analytics platforms.
Experience establishing or maturing a multi-country revenue growth management capability across multiple channels, customer segments, and business models.

For details on our Equity, Diversity & Inclusion commitment, please click here.

We’re committed to attracting and retaining passionate individuals to help create a healthier future. That’s why SickKids Foundation is looking for a new Associate Director, Development Analytics.

Description Of The Position

Fundraising is a sales function. It has a pipeline, defined stages, conversion rates, cycle times and coverage ratios—and a frontline team whose time is one of the organization’s scarcest resources.

The Associate Director, Development Analytics owns the analytics behind that pipeline. The role makes fundraising performance visible and measurable, identifies where opportunities exist to improve it, and translates those insights into clear, actionable recommendations for fundraising leaders.

This is a hands-on role for a sales and pipeline analytics professional. The successful candidate is comfortable working directly with data, building reporting and dashboards, and developing analytical or predictive models when they add value. But the role goes beyond producing reports and models. Its real value is in the analysis: knowing which metrics matter, identifying where the pipeline is performing well or breaking down, uncovering opportunities within fundraiser portfolios, and helping leaders understand what actions they can take as a result.

The role also connects Research Services with frontline fundraising. It translates prospect intelligence and analytical signals into clear, prioritized opportunities so fundraisers can focus their time and effort on the prospects with the greatest potential.

The Associate Director, Development Analytics is a key role within the Business Intelligence & Analytics team. Reporting directly to the Director, Development Analytics, you will provide functional leadership for Development Analytics, serve as the authoritative advisor to Development leadership, and partner across the analytics function: with Data Science & Engineering to ensure development data is well modelled and accessible, with Research Services to turn prospect intelligence into action, and with Marketing Analytics to build end-to-end visibility from donor acquisition through the development pipeline.

You will play a central role in delivering the Foundation's Data & Analytics Strategy (DAS) for Development, setting the analytics roadmap, standards and priorities and executing key use cases that build analytics maturity and drive measurable value for fundraising and the broader organization.

Key Responsibilities

Functional Leadership & Roadmap

Provide functional leadership for Development Analytics, integrating pipeline, portfolio, revenue, campaign and donor analytics across Development.
Establish and maintain the Development Analytics roadmap, operating model, methodologies, standards and tools within the approved Development strategy and the DAS.
Own the development analytics intake process: prioritize, approve, defer or redirect analytics requests so that priorities are clear, timelines are met and the team is set up to deliver with consistency and quality.
Serve as the authoritative advisor to Development leadership on forecasting, portfolio optimization, prospect strategy, performance measurement and the effective allocation of fundraising resources.
Maintain and enforce analytics processes and standards, and hold stakeholders accountable for agreed data inputs and business requirements.
Measure and report on the adoption and impact of analytics products.
Resolve conflicting business requirements, data limitations and competing analytical priorities across Development, determining when existing approaches should be adapted or replaced.
Anticipate emerging business needs and initiate analytical work that may challenge current assumptions, practices or resource-allocation decisions.

Pipeline, Portfolio & Performance Analytics

Own development pipeline analytics: stage progression, conversion and win rates, cycle time and velocity, coverage ratios, average gift size and slippage, by fundraiser, portfolio, segment and campaign.
Independently identify and frame where the funnel is underperforming and why, including emerging issues where the problem and approach are not yet defined, and bring forward specific, prioritized recommendations rather than describing the numbers.
Partner with fundraising leadership on portfolio construction and optimization: right-sizing portfolios, balancing prospect capacity against fundraiser bandwidth, surfacing under-worked or misassigned prospects, and analyzing frontline productivity to improve return on fundraiser time.
Establish Development-wide KPI definitions and analytical standards for pipeline, portfolio, revenue and fundraiser-performance reporting, within enterprise data-governance requirements, so leadership, Finance and the lines of business work from one trusted set of numbers.
Build, maintain and evolve self-serve dashboards and automated reporting tools that allow fundraising teams to access portfolio insights and performance data independently to make faster decisions.
Translate complex findings into clear narratives, presentations and recommendations for non-technical audiences.

Advanced Analytics & Predictive Modelling

Build and deploy predictive models such as propensity to give, upgrade likelihood, lapse prediction, segmentation and lifetime value (LTV) to inform portfolio strategy, prospect prioritization and the allocation of fundraising resources.
Lead revenue forecasting and in-year reforecasting with weighted pipeline analysis and scenario modelling, clearly articulating risk and upside.

Team Leadership & Coaching

Create a culture of curiosity, quality and continuous improvement by generously sharing knowledge across the team, introducing better ways to approach data analysis, building models and interpreting findings to raise the overall quality of analytical output.

Experience designing and building self-serve dashboards and automated reporting frameworks.

About BERMANFALK Hospitality Group

BERMANFALK Hospitality Group delivers custom casegoods and seating to the hospitality industry, including hotels, resorts, and restaurants; primarily focused on the 3+ to 5 star market. We manage every project from design phase, approvals and shop drawings through to manufacturing, quality control, logistics, delivery and installation. Our model depends on a trusted network of manufacturing partners, which makes precise cost control, disciplined project accounting, and sound supply-chain ﬁnance central to our success.
We are growing and evolving high paced business, and we are looking for a ﬁnance leader who can run rigorous day-to-day project and cost accounting while shaping the ﬁnancial strategy that will carry the company to its next stage.

ROLE SUMMARY

The Director, Finance & Accounting is the senior ﬁnance leader at BERMANFALK and owns every part of the company's ﬁnancial function. The role has two equal halves:

Operational ﬁnance:
building and running cost-based and project-based accounting so that every project's true cost, margin, and cash position is known in real time, from quote to ﬁnal invoice.
Strategic ﬁnance:
leading ﬁnancial planning, capital structure, banking relationships, risk management, and growth strategy for the company as a whole.

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who is as comfortable reconciling a landed-cost variance on a guestroom package as presenting a ﬁve-year plan to ownership and lenders.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Project & Job-Cost Accounting

Own the full project accounting lifecycle, including project setup, budgets, cost tracking, change orders, billing, and close-out.
Design and maintain a job-costing structure that captures manufacturer costs, freight, duties, brokerage, warehousing, installation, samples, and allocated overhead by project and by line item.
Ensure change orders and scope changes are priced, approved, and billed promptly so that margin does not erode.
Deliver project proﬁtability reporting that compares estimated and actual results, identiﬁes variances, and feeds lessons back into estimating.

Cost Accounting & Supply-Chain Finance

Build accurate landed-cost models for outsourced production, covering FOB pricing, ocean and inland freight, tariffs and duties, customs brokerage, insurance, and FX.
Partner with procurement to manage manufacturer deposits, payment milestones, letters of credit, and supplier terms.
Monitor and mitigate foreign-exchange exposure on supplier payments and customer contracts, including hedging strategy where appropriate.
Track tariff and trade-policy changes and model their impact on pricing, sourcing decisions, and open contracts.
Support estimating and sales with cost data, pricing models, and margin guardrails for bids and proposals.
Evaluate manufacturing partners from a ﬁnancial perspective, including cost competitiveness, ﬁnancial stability, and risk concentration.

Financial Operations & Controls

Lead month-end and year-end close, producing accurate and timely ﬁnancial statements.
Prepare consolidated Balance Sheets, Income Statements, and Cash Flow Statements.
Coordinate and lead all annual external audits, ensuring robust internal controls and GAAP/IFRS compliance.
Maintain 13-week cash-ﬂow forecasting and working-capital management across overlapping projects.
Maintain direct oversight over global banking accounts and treasury management across 4 countries.
Oversee Indirect Tax Compliance & Remittances – US Sales & Use Tax, Canadian provincial and federal sales taxes and UK VAT returns.
Lead corporate income tax compliance and statutory filings with the CRA, IRS and HMRC.

Strategic Finance & Leadership

Develop and own the annual budget, rolling forecasts, and long-range ﬁnancial plan.
Serve as a strategic advisor to the Executive Team and ownership on growth, pricing strategy, market expansion, and investment decisions.
Build KPI dashboards covering backlog, gross margin by project and client, projects rolling forecast.
Evaluate strategic opportunities including new product categories, partnerships, acquisitions, and vertical integration.
Lead the selection, implementation, or optimization of ERP and project accounting systems that connect estimating, procurement, and ﬁnance.
Build, mentor, and lead the ﬁnance and accounting team as the company scales.
Establish standard operating procedures (SOPs), clear performance metrics, and workflow efficiency across global finance functions.

QUALIFICATIONS

Required

CPA designation (Canada) or equivalent professional accounting credential is preferred.
10+ years of progressive ﬁnance experience, including at least 5 years in a senior leadership role (Controller, Director of Finance, or VP Finance).
Deep, hands-on expertise in project-based and job-cost accounting, WIP reporting, and percentage-of-completion or milestone revenue recognition.
Experience in manufacturing, contract furniture, FF&E, millwork, construction, or another project-driven industry.
Working knowledge of import/export ﬁnance, including landed costs, duties, FX, and international supplier payments.
Proven experience managing banking relationships, credit facilities, and cash-ﬂow planning.
Strong command of ﬁnancial modelling and advanced Excel, plus experience with ERP or project accounting systems.
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain ﬁnancial results to project managers, sales teams, and ownership alike.

﻿Preferred

Experience with outsourced or offshore manufacturing (e.g., Asia, Mexico, Europe) and the related supply-chain ﬁnance.
Background in the hospitality FF&E, contract furniture, or hotel development sector.
Experience leading an ERP implementation.
Familiarity with FX hedging, trade credit insurance, letters of credit, and surety bonding.
Experience in a privately held or family-owned company during a period of growth.

What Success Looks Like in the First Year

Every active project has an accurate, current cost-to-complete and margin forecast.
Month-end close is completed on a consistent, reliable timeline with project-level reporting.
Landed-cost and pricing models are standardized and used by estimating on every bid.
A rolling cash-ﬂow forecast and KPI dashboard are in place and reviewed with leadership regularly.
A clear multi-year ﬁnancial strategy and systems roadmap has been presented to and adopted by ownership.

Why Join BERMANFALK

A senior seat at the leadership table with direct inﬂuence on the company's direction.
The opportunity to build and shape the ﬁnance function of a growing hospitality business.
Work on high-proﬁle projects across the hospitality sector on a global scale.
Competitive compensation, performance bonus, and beneﬁts package.

COMPENSATION:
Salary Range: $150,000 - $175,000 CAD per year

BENEFITS

Comprehensive extended health & dental benefits plan with a health spending account
Paid time off including vacation
Flexible working environment - Hybrid & Remote option depending on the role
Supplementary maternity and parental leave top-up
Beautiful open office space in Langley with full kitchen - offering coffee, snacks and refreshments
Tuition reimbursement program and various growth opportunities
Casual dress
Company social events and fun team-bonding activities
Employee assistance programs

Our business is guided by honesty and integrity. We offer competitive wages and a progressive, collaborative and creative work environment. While we laugh a great deal, we have high expectations of each other, and top-level performance is essential.
BERMANFALK Hospitality Group is an equal opportunity employer.

office or remotely based on the specific needs of the company. We feel this model empowers employees to work where they feel most productive, while maintaining a strong connection with their team and encouraging company-wide collaboration.

Step into a senior leadership role offering a competitive $100,000 to $150,000 annual salary, negotiable based on qualifications, plus excellent benefits!

Build the systems, teams, and financial stability that will support the Nation for the next decade

About Curve Lake First Nation

Curve Lake First Nation is an Anishinaabe community with deep roots in this territory, grounded in relationships to land, water, and each other as Curve Lakers. Known historically as Mud Lake, Curve Lake continues as a living, resilient Nation of almost 3,000 members. As part of the Michi Saagiig Anishinaabeg and signatories to the Williams Treaties, the community carries forward its responsibilities, teachings, and governance systems. Curve Lake is a place of strong kinship, cultural continuity, and collective responsibility, where each member contributes to the wellbeing of the Nation. Our community is located just north of the City of Peterborough, Ontario.

Home to trailblazers like Elsie Knott, Canada's first Anishinaabe Kwe O'gimaa, and renowned artisans, our community blends rich history with vibrant culture. More than an employer, we're a community of choice. Join us in preserving traditions, fostering diversity, and contributing to a future where old ways merge seamlessly with progress. Shape the legacy of Curve Lake—a place where heritage meets opportunity.

To learn more about us, please visit: curvelakefirstnation.ca

About the Opportunity

Curve Lake First Nation has an exciting opportunity for a full-time, permanent Director of Finance and Administration
, based in Curve Lake, Ontario.
This role joins the organization during a period of organizational transition and growth.

Reporting to the Executive Director, you will provide strategic leadership across the Nation’s corporate functions. These are financial governance, human resources, policy and planning, communications, and information technology. Finance sits at the heart of the role. You will be accountable for sound financial oversight, audit readiness, and strong relationships with funders, auditors, and the First Nations Financial Management Board.

Where We Are Now

The Nation is strengthening its administrative foundations; you will provide interim oversight and stabilization across Finance, HR, IT, and Policy and Planning while building out your team. You will also lead the selection and implementation of a new Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system.

A key priority is moving the Nation from year-by-year funding to Indigenous Services Canada’s 10-year grant. This means completing the Financial Management Board certification process and putting the controls and reporting in place to qualify. Predictable, long-term funding will give the Nation far greater confidence in its forecasting and planning.

What Success Looks Like

In your first year, success will mean a fully staffed division with your managers in place, trusted relationships with Chief and Council, staff, and community, strengthened audit readiness and internal controls, and the ERP selection well underway.

By the end of year two, you will have led the Nation through FMB certification and embedded consistent financial, governance, and administrative practices. You will also have put systems in place that keep reporting and audits on schedule, giving the organization a solid foundation for the years ahead.

Your responsibilities include, but are not limited to:
Leading multi-year financial planning, forecasting, and annual operating and capital budgets
Serving as executive lead for external audits, including selecting the appropriate audit firm and working closely with auditors throughout the process
Ensuring compliance with funding agreements, Indigenous Services Canada reporting requirements, and the Nation’s Financial Administration Law
Leading the Nation through the FMB certification and 10-year grant process
Structuring and staffing the finance function so reporting deadlines are consistently met, working with bookkeepers, analysts, and account managers
Providing executive oversight of HR, IT, policy and planning, and communications through four direct-report managers
Overseeing the selection and implementation of an ERP system, along with cybersecurity, data governance, and digital modernization
Providing financial analysis, risk advice, and recommendations to the Executive Director and Chief and Council

Due to the role's significance, refer to the Director of Finance and Administration document for a comprehensive overview beyond the listed duties.

More About You

To qualify, you will need a post-secondary degree or diploma in finance, accounting, or a related financial field
, along with at least 7 years of senior-level experience in financial administration or corporate services,
including experience working within a First Nation organization.

The following are required:
A valid Class G Driver’s Licence
Ability to undergo a criminal background check and vulnerable sector check
Willingness and ability to travel as required

The following skills and experience will be strong assets:
Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation
Certified Aboriginal Financial Manager (CAFM) or Certified Aboriginal Professional Administrator (CAPA) designation
A master’s degree in public administration, finance, or a related field
Direct experience with the First Nations Financial Management Board, FMB certification, or the 10-year grant process
Strong working knowledge of audit processes, GAAP, and funder reporting requirements
Experience working with Indigenous Services Canada and other funding agencies
Experience overseeing multiple functional areas such as Finance, HR, IT, and Planning

As our ideal candidate, you are a disciplined, systems-minded leader who keeps deadlines met and audits clean, and who knows how to build a finance team organized around its reporting obligations. Your understanding of First Nation finances runs from day-to-day funding agreements through to the path toward long-term grant funding. Just as importantly, you lead with integrity, calm, and a people-centred approach, bringing an awareness of intergenerational trauma and its impact on workplaces and governance, along with a genuine respect for Curve Lake First Nation’s history, culture, and traditions.

Note: Preference will be given to applicants who have First Nation or Indigenous ancestry.

About the Benefits

In exchange for your hard work and dedication, you will receive a highly competitive salary of $100,000 to $150,000
negotiable dependent on experience, along with a great host of benefits, including:
Relocation assistance
Comprehensive Benefits Plan: extended health care, dental, vision, life and long-term disability, etc.
Competitive Pension Plan with up to 7.5% employer matching
40 paid hours for Special/Personal Leave Bereavement Leave
Paid time off for 17 designated days, including National Indigenous Day, Christmas Day, etc.
Generous vacation accrual
Paid sick days
Regular community events such as Pow Wows, Harvesters' Gatherings, Christmas Craft Shows, and more!

Take on a senior leadership role that builds lasting financial stability and strong systems for the Curve Lake First Nation community. Apply now!

Curve Lake First Nation is an Anishinaabe community with deep roots in this territory, grounded in relationships to land, water, and each other as Curve Lakers. Known historically as Mud Lake, Curve Lake continues as a living, resilient Nation of almost 3,000 members. As part of the Michi Saagiig Anishinaabeg and signatories to the Williams Treaties, the community carries forward its responsibilities, teachings, and governance systems. Curve Lake is a place of strong kinship, cultural continuity, and collective responsibility, where each member contributes to the wellbeing of the Nation. Our community is located just north of the City of Peterborough, Ontario.

Home to trailblazers like Elsie Knott, Canada's first Anishinaabe Kwe O'gimaa, and renowned artisans, our community blends rich history with vibrant culture. More than an employer, we're a community of choice. Join us in preserving traditions, fostering diversity, and contributing to a future where old ways merge seamlessly with progress. Shape the legacy of Curve Lake—a place where heritage meets opportunity.

To learn more about us, please visit: curvelakefirstnation.ca

About the Opportunity

Curve Lake First Nation has an exciting opportunity for a full-time, permanent Director of Finance and Administration
, based in Curve Lake, Ontario.
This role joins the organization during a period of organizational transition and growth.

Reporting to the Executive Director, you will provide strategic leadership across the Nation’s corporate functions.
